newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 22.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Meetings between coalition chairmen concerning changes in the cabinet will continue today and will be joined by President Vaclav Havel. The leaders agreed yesterday only that changes are necessary, but have not agreed on the extent.

- The leader of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), Milos Zeman, presented his proposal to revive the economy. CSSD's plan is to support exporters with tax breaks, increase support of farmers, increase consumer taxes and introduce import surcharges.
- The cabinet met with heavy criticism from the opposition in parliament yesterday with its report on the government budget during the first quarter of the year.
- The cabinet decided yesterday that pensions would increase on average by 10.5 percent from August.

- According to a report from the agency Factum, 23 percent of Czechs believe that the quality of health care has worsened in the past three years, 16 percent believe the opposite and 55 percent believe it stayed the same. For the next three years, 37 percent believe health care will get worse, and 13.5 percent believe it will improve.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Developments with the rate of the crown have also manifested themselves on the price of securities on the Prague Stock Exchange. After a drop of nearly three percent on Tuesday, the price level on the exchange, measured by its index PX 50 fell another 2.6 percent.
- March revenue from transportation had another year-on-year drop this time by 3.1 percent. The drop for the entire first quarter is 5.8 percent.

- From last July until the end of this June, the Agriculture Ministry estimates grain imports of 801,000 tonnes, which is 11.5 percent of domestic demand. In the same time the year before, only 127,000 tonnes were imported.

- Entry into the company Exportni Prumyslova a.s., which was established about one month ago, should be confirmed by shareholders of Spolchemie and Zelezarny a Dratovny Bohumin by the end of next week.
- Kaucuk Kralupy nad Vltavou a.s., a leading domestic petrochemical producer, had gross profits of 58 million crowns during the first quarter of this year. It had total revenue of 1.4 billion crowns.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The general director of IPB bank, Jiri Tesar, who was released from jail yesterday, announced that he will leave his post at the end of June. His departure is not connected to the case of alleged fraud which he and his deputy are facing.
- Three of the 11 former members of the management of Agrobanka were released from jail. The investigation continues.
- The cabinet decided yesterday that it will settle the problem of Cedok's six billion crown debts from the time of its privatisation outside court.
- The European Commission began a programme to help domestic companies with exports through the Exporters' Support Fund, into which it will deposit 100 million crowns as part of the PHARE programme.
PRAVO - The cabinet decided yesterday on the direct sale of 73 percent of Crystalex Novy Bor to the company Porcela Plus.

- According to a law for social support which the cabinet approved yesterday, the amount of social support and the number of people who receive it should increase, provided the law is approved by parliament.

- For the third time since the beginning of the week, CSOB increased its interest rates, this time on two-week deposits and monthly deposits. Foresbank announced on Wednesday that it would introduce rapid-return deposits, Banka Hana increased its reference rate to 22 percent, IPB's basic rate will increase to 17.3 percent today and its basic interest rate to 21.3.
